data.second_finding: lower_bound_on_joint_error is not a lower bound: human fallibility biases beta-hat down, verifier pre-filtering biases it up, and two unmeasured biases in opposite directions do not compose into a bound. data.defect: I wrote six consecutive events with invented timestamps. I advanced a plausible monotone clock in my head instead of reading one.
data.drift: up to 2h15m ahead of the wall clock, monotone and therefore plausible
data.corrected_how: the log is append-only and a prefix digest covers committed positions, so the wrong entries are NOT rewritten. This event is the correction, and the affected entries are enumerated above.
data.also_wrong: two Slack posts headed 06:00 and 06:30 (actual ~03:55 and ~04:05), and the incident report's stated discovery time, which is corrected in place because that file was written minutes earlier and is not append-only
data.what_is_unaffected: every substantive finding. The EXP-31 interleaving rests on the probe fingerprint alternating across seven commits and on 5 disagreements in 22 overlapping cells, neither of which involves wall-clock. The beta axis defect rests on arithmetic. Ordering of events is also unaffected, since the fabricated stamps were monotone.
data.how_it_evaded_the_instrument: validate() checks the FORMAT of ts and requires an explicit offset - both impeccable here - and never asks whether the value is true. A format check on a timestamp is not a check on a timestamp.
data.ratchet: events.append() now rejects a ts more than 15 minutes from the wall clock, with five tests. It runs at append only, never in validate, because reading a historical log must not depend on when it is read - the same reason ts requires an explicit offset.
data.note: the irony is the point: this happened in the same hour I documented an experiment runner ignoring its own project's append-only invariant. The instrument that would have caught me did not exist because nobody had imagined the author being the unreliable party.

data.what_survives: the axis defect itself, now with three independent hand-verifications and reproducing arithmetic. It was simply there to be found by anyone who read mine_beta.py:158 against beta.py:172.
data.what_does_not: any claim that difference-of-model-family produced it. Nothing about Whewell's second clause was demonstrated. This project has no measured evidence that difference-of-class does anything for it, which is where it was yesterday.
data.structural_lesson: you cannot run a blind experiment inside the repository you are writing your findings into. The trajectory is append-only, committed, and the first thing a thorough agent reads, so every finding recorded there joins the corpus for every subsequent run. Future independence tests need a frozen snapshot taken before the first arm runs, and the angle text committed - an unrecorded prompt makes no arm's result interpretable.

control_findings_verified_here.min_rejections: MIN_REJECTIONS=30 is exactly one below 31, the smallest n at which even a flawless record's Wilson upper bound clears beta*=0.111. Recomputed: 0/30 -> 0.11352 fails, 0/31 -> 0.11026 clears. Realistic requirement 48/62/137/368/3045 at true beta 0.02/0.04/0.06/0.08/0.10, and never at or above 0.111. EXP-01's two corrected estimates, 0.12 and 0.14, both sit above beta* itself.
control_findings_verified_here.fair_statement: the constant is not a bug - it gates the measured verdict, not a routing claim. What the arithmetic shows is that no routing decision can ever be taken at the evidence floor as set, and neither the code nor the spec says so.

claim_1.arithmetic: frac_seen = p_good + (1-p_good)(1-recall) <= 1, so T_eff <= T_r and n_max >= T_a/T_r = 25/8 = 3.125 for every recall and therefore every beta, including beta = 1.0. The gate asks whether a quantity with a floor of 3.125 exceeds 1.
claim_1.consequence: Gate B2 is the only gate condition whose value depends on beta. Every other condition asks whether something exists, ran or completed. So beta is not load-bearing on any decision the gate system makes.
claim_1.the_adr_states_a_false_belief_about_its_: ADR-0015: 'If measured critic recall yields a ceiling of 1, orchestration provides no throughput at all.' Recall only ever raises n_max above the cycle-to-review floor; it has no path to lowering it.
claim_1.second_defect: the ceiling table 3.1 to 5.5 is tagged [algebra], but the numbers are that formula evaluated on three unmeasured point estimates - T_a=25, T_r=8, p_good=0.55. Algebra evaluated on invented inputs is not algebra about the world, and working principle 2 applies.

claim_2.claim: the retrospective mining route cannot supply beta's denominator because --state merged makes every row an accept
claim_2.verdict: PARTLY - right outcome, wrong mechanism, and the real reason is worse
claim_2.real_reason: there is no pipeline at all. mine_beta.py writes private JSON that nothing in src/consilience reads; beta.py explicitly forbids proxy labels and mine_beta.py produces nothing but proxy labels; and the two compute different quantities from disjoint sources.
claim_2.reframes_the_axis_defect: it is not only that mine_beta.py conditions the wrong way round - even conditioned correctly its output could not reach compute(), because proxy labels are inadmissible by design and no path exists for them to travel

claim_3.claim: beta* is in neither the specification nor the code
claim_3.confirmed: zero occurrences in docs/40-spec/v0-draft.md and zero in src/consilience; nothing in the code compares a measured beta against any threshold
claim_3.refuted: the claim said it lives in research notes and one ADR; it is in three ADRs plus seven design documents and three context documents
claim_3.honest_reading: thoroughly documented and entirely absent from the two artefacts that would make it operative. Defensible today because the observe-only increment has no routing surface and a test enforces that; a defect the moment one lands.

data.what_it_adds_up_to: the meter has never received a row of input; the experiment that produces beta cannot reach the meter that computes it; the only gate that consumes beta cannot be moved by it; and the threshold beta is compared against exists in no executable form. The thesis is not wrong, it is untested - which is what the pre-spec phase is for, and all four are cheaper to fix now than after a routing surface exists.
data.recommended_order: wire the meter's input first, because everything else is downstream of having any beta at all; then fix Gate B2's condition, because a gate that cannot fail is worse than no gate - it manufactures the appearance of a check
